submenus.description: Contributes submenu items to the editor

id.description: Identifier of the menu to display as a submenu.

label.description: The label of the menu item which leads to this submenu.

icon.description: (Optional) Icon which is used to represent the submenu in the UI. Either a file path, an object with file paths for dark and light themes, or a theme icon references, like "\$(zap)"

fileMatch.description: The file pattern (or an array of patterns) to match, for example "package.json" or "*.launch". Exclusion patterns start with '!'

url.description: A schema URL ('http:', 'https:') or relative path to the extension folder ('./').

extensions.description: File extensions associated to the language.

filenames.description: File names associated to the language.

filenamePatterns.description: File name glob patterns associated to the language.

mimetypes.description: Mime types associated to the language.

firstLine.description: A regular expression matching the first line of a file of the language.

configuration.description: A relative path to a file containing configuration options for the language.

icon.description: A icon to use as file icon, if no icon theme provides one for the language.

language.description: Language identifier for which this syntax is contributed to.

scopeName.description: Textmate scope name used by the tmLanguage file.

path.description: Path of the tmLanguage file. The path is relative to the extension folder and typically starts with './syntaxes/'.

embeddedLanguages.description: A map of scope name to language id if this grammar contains embedded languages.

tokenTypes.description: A map of scope name to token types.

injectTo.description: List of language scope names to which this grammar is injected to.

balancedBracketScopes.description: Defines which scope names contain balanced brackets.

unbalancedBracketScopes.description: Defines which scope names do not contain balanced brackets.

language.description: Language identifier for which this snippet is contributed to.

path.description: Path of the snippets file. The path is relative to the extension folder and typically starts with './snippets/'.

id.description: The identifier of the semantic token type
id.patternErrorMessage: Identifiers should be in the form letterOrDigit[_-letterOrDigit]*

superType.description: The super type of the semantic token type
superType.patternErrorMessage: Super types should be in the form letterOrDigit[_-letterOrDigit]*

description.description: The description of the semantic token type

id.description: The identifier of the semantic token modifier
id.patternErrorMessage: Identifiers should be in the form letterOrDigit[_-letterOrDigit]*

description.description: The description of the semantic token modifier

language.description: Lists the languge for which the defaults are.

scopes.description: Maps a semantic token (described by semantic token selector) to one or more textMate scopes used to represent that token.

id.description: Id of the color theme as used in the user settings.

label.description: Label of the color theme as shown in the UI.

uiTheme.markdownDescription: Base theme defining the colors around the editor: `vs` is the light color theme, `vs-dark` is the dark color theme. `hc-black` is the dark high contrast theme, `hc-light` is the light high contrast theme.

path.markdownDescription: Path of the tmTheme file. The path is relative to the extension folder and is typically `./colorthemes/awesome-color-theme.json`.

id.description: Id of the file icon theme as used in the user settings.

label.description: Label of the file icon theme as shown in the UI.

path.description: Path of the file icon theme definition file. The path is relative to the extension folder and is typically './fileicons/awesome-icon-theme.json'.

id.description: Id of the product icon theme as used in the user settings.

label.description: Label of the product icon theme as shown in the UI.

path.description: Path of the product icon theme definition file. The path is relative to the extension folder and is typically './producticons/awesome-product-icon-theme.json'.

id.description: The identifier of the themable color
id.patternErrorMessage: Identifiers must only contain letters, digits and dots and can not start with a dot

description.description: The description of the themable color

light.description: The default color for light themes. Either a color value in hex (#RRGGBB[AA]) or the identifier of a themable color which provides the default.

dark.description: The default color for dark themes. Either a color value in hex (#RRGGBB[AA]) or the identifier of a themable color which provides the default.

highContrast.description: The default color for high contrast dark themes. Either a color value in hex (#RRGGBB[AA]) or the identifier of a themable color which provides the default. If not provided, the `dark` color is used as default for high contrast dark themes.

highContrastLight.description: The default color for high contrast light themes. Either a color value in hex (#RRGGBB[AA]) or the identifier of a themable color which provides the default. If not provided, the `light` color is used as default for high contrast light themes.

propertyNames.description: The identifier of the themable icon
propertyNames.patternErrorMessage: Identifiers can only contain letters, digits and minuses and need to consist of at least two segments in the form `component-iconname`.

description.description: The description of the themable icon

Use this to register a data provider through `vscode.window.registerTreeDataProviderForView` API. Also to trigger activating your extension by registering `onView:${id}` event to `activationEvents`.

allOf.description: Contributed views welcome content. Welcome content will be rendered in tree based views whenever they have no meaningful content to display, ie. the File Explorer when no folder is open. Such content is useful as in-product documentation to drive users to use certain features before they are available. A good example would be a `Clone Repository` button in the File Explorer welcome view.

items.description: Contributed welcome content for a specific view.

anyOf.description: Target view identifier for this welcome content. Only tree based views are supported.
Target view identifier for this welcome content. Only tree based views are supported.

contents.description: Welcome content to be displayed. The format of the contents is a subset of Markdown, with support for links only.

when.description: Condition when the welcome content should be displayed.

group.description: Group to which this welcome content belongs. Proposed API.

enablement.description: Condition when the welcome content buttons and command links should be enabled.

walkthroughs.description: Contribute walkthroughs to help users getting started with your extension.

icon.description: Relative path to the icon of the walkthrough. The path is relative to the extension location. If not specified, the icon defaults to the extension icon if available.

featuredFor.description: Walkthroughs that match one of these glob patterns appear as 'featured' in workspaces with the specified files. For example, a walkthrough for TypeScript projects might specify `tsconfig.json` here.

when.description: Context key expression to control the visibility of this walkthrough.

steps.description: Steps to complete as part of this walkthrough.

id.description: Unique identifier for this step. This is used to keep track of which steps have been completed.

description.description: Description of step. Supports ``preformatted``, __italic__, and **bold** text. Use markdown-style links for commands or external links: [Title](command:myext.command), [Title](command:toSide:myext.command), or [Title](https://aka.ms). Links on their own line will be rendered as buttons.

button.deprecationMessage: Deprecated. Use markdown links in the description instead, i.e. [Title](command:myext.command), [Title](command:toSide:myext.command), or [Title](https://aka.ms)

media.description: Media to show alongside this step, either an image or markdown content.

image.description: Path to an image - or object consisting of paths to light, dark, and hc images - relative to extension directory. Depending on context, the image will be displayed from 400px to 800px wide, with similar bounds on height. To support HIDPI displays, the image will be rendered at 1.5x scaling, for example a 900 physical pixels wide image will be displayed as 600 logical pixels wide.

dark.description: Path to the image for dark themes, relative to extension directory.

light.description: Path to the image for light themes, relative to extension directory.

hc.description: Path to the image for hc themes, relative to extension directory.

hcLight.description: Path to the image for hc light themes, relative to extension directory.

svg.description: Path to an svg, color tokens are supported in variables to support theming to match the workbench.

markdown.description: Path to the markdown document, relative to extension directory.

completionEvents.description: Events that should trigger this step to become checked off. If empty or not defined, the step will check off when any of the step's buttons or links are clicked; if the step has no buttons or links it will check on when it is selected.

defaultSnippets.label: onCommand
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step when a given command is executed anywhere in VS Code.

defaultSnippets.label: onLink
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step when a given link is opened via a walkthrough step.

defaultSnippets.label: onView
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step when a given view is opened

defaultSnippets.label: onSettingChanged
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step when a given setting is changed

defaultSnippets.label: onContext
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step when a context key expression is true.

defaultSnippets.label: onExtensionInstalled
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step when an extension with the given id is installed. If the extension is already installed, the step will start off checked.

defaultSnippets.label: onStepSelected
defaultSnippets.description: Check off step as soon as it is selected.

doneOn.description: Signal to mark step as complete.
doneOn.deprecationMessage: doneOn is deprecated. By default steps will be checked off when their buttons are clicked, to configure further use completionEvents

command.description: Mark step done when the specified command is executed.

when.description: Context key expression to control the visibility of this step.

viewType.markdownDescription: Identifier for the custom editor. This must be unique across all custom editors, so we recommend including your extension id as part of `viewType`. The `viewType` is used when registering custom editors with `vscode.registerCustomEditorProvider` and in the `onCustomEditor:${id}` [activation event](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/references/activation-events).

displayName.description: Human readable name of the custom editor. This is displayed to users when selecting which editor to use.

selector.description: Set of globs that the custom editor is enabled for.

filenamePattern.description: Glob that the custom editor is enabled for.

priority.markdownDescription: Controls if the custom editor is enabled automatically when the user opens a file, diff, or merge editor. This may be overridden by users using the `workbench.editorAssociations` or `workbench.diffEditorAssociations` setting.

markdownEnumDescriptions: The editor is automatically used when the user opens a resource, provided that no other default custom editors are registered for that resource.
The editor is not automatically used when the user opens a resource, but a user can switch to the editor using the `Reopen With` command.
The editor is automatically used when the user opens a resource, provided that no other default custom editors are registered for that resource.

textEditor.markdownDescription: Controls if the custom editor is enabled automatically when the user opens a file. This is the base value: when `diffEditor` or `mergeEditor` are not specified, they fall back to this value.

markdownEnumDescriptions: The editor is automatically used when the user opens a resource, provided that no other default custom editors are registered for that resource.
The editor is not automatically used when the user opens a resource, but a user can switch to the editor using the `Reopen With` command.
diffEditor.markdownDescription: Controls if the custom editor is enabled automatically when the user opens a diff. When not specified, the value of `textEditor` is used.

markdownEnumDescriptions: The editor is automatically used when the user opens a resource, provided that no other default custom editors are registered for that resource.
The editor is not automatically used when the user opens a resource, but a user can switch to the editor using the `Reopen With` command.
mergeEditor.markdownDescription: Controls if the custom editor is enabled automatically when the user opens a merge editor. When not specified, the value of `textEditor` is used.

displayName.description: Human readable name of the notebook.

selector.description: Set of globs that the notebook is for.

filenamePattern.description: Glob that the notebook is enabled for.

excludeFileNamePattern.description: Glob that the notebook is disabled for.

id.description: Unique identifier of the notebook output renderer.

displayName.description: Human readable name of the notebook output renderer.

dependencies.markdownDescription: List of kernel dependencies the renderer requires. If any of the dependencies are present in the `NotebookKernel.preloads`, the renderer can be used.

optionalDependencies.markdownDescription: List of soft kernel dependencies the renderer can make use of. If any of the dependencies are present in the `NotebookKernel.preloads`, the renderer will be preferred over renderers that don't interact with the kernel.

enumDescriptions: Messaging is required. The renderer will only be used when it's part of an extension that can be run in an extension host.
The renderer is better with messaging available, but it's not required.
The renderer does not require messaging.
requiresMessaging.description: Defines how and if the renderer needs to communicate with an extension host, via `createRendererMessaging`. Renderers with stronger messaging requirements may not work in all environments.

mimeTypes.description: Set of globs that the notebook is for.

entrypoint.description: File to load in the webview to render the extension.
File to load in the webview to render the extension.

extends.description: Existing renderer that this one extends.

path.description: File to load in the webview to render the extension.

type.description: Unique identifier for this debug adapter.

label.description: Display name for this debug adapter.

program.description: Path to the debug adapter program. Path is either absolute or relative to the extension folder.

args.description: Optional arguments to pass to the adapter.

runtime.description: Optional runtime in case the program attribute is not an executable but requires a runtime.

variables.description: Mapping from interactive variables (e.g. ${action.pickProcess}) in `launch.json` to a command.

languages.description: List of languages for which the debug extension could be considered the "default debugger".

configurationSnippets.description: Snippets for adding new configurations in 'launch.json'.

when.description: Condition which must be true to enable this type of debugger. Consider using 'shellExecutionSupported', 'virtualWorkspace', 'resourceScheme' or an extension-defined context key as appropriate for this.

hiddenWhen.description: When this condition is true, this debugger type is hidden from the debugger list, but is still enabled.

deprecated.description: Optional message to mark this debug type as being deprecated.

strings.description: UI strings contributed by this debug adapter.

unverifiedBreakpoints.description: When there are unverified breakpoints in a language supported by this debug adapter, this message will appear on the breakpoint hover and in the breakpoints view. Markdown and command links are supported.

when.description: Condition which must be true to enable breakpoints in this language. Consider matching this to the debugger when clause as appropriate.

type.description: The actual task type. Please note that types starting with a '$' are reserved for internal usage.

required.markdownDescription: The names of the properties from the `properties` object that must be provided for a task of this type to be considered a match. Used by VS Code to associate a `tasks.json` entry with a registered task provider.

properties.description: Additional properties of the task type

when.markdownDescription: Condition which must be true to enable this type of task. Consider using `shellExecutionSupported`, `processExecutionSupported`, and `customExecutionSupported` as appropriate for this task definition. See the [API documentation](https://code.visualstudio.com/api/extension-guides/task-provider#when-clause) for more information.

base.description: The name of a base problem matcher to use.

owner.description: The owner of the problem inside Code. Can be omitted if base is specified. Defaults to 'external' if omitted and base is not specified.

source.description: A human-readable string describing the source of this diagnostic, e.g. 'typescript' or 'super lint'.

severity.description: The default severity for captures problems. Is used if the pattern doesn't define a match group for severity.

applyTo.description: Controls if a problem reported on a text document is applied only to open, closed or all documents.

anyOf.description: The name of a contributed or predefined pattern

pattern.description: A problem pattern or the name of a contributed or predefined problem pattern. Can be omitted if base is specified.

fileLocation.description: Defines how file names reported in a problem pattern should be interpreted. A relative fileLocation may be an array, where the second element of the array is the path of the relative file location. The search fileLocation mode, performs a deep (and, possibly, heavy) file system search within the directories specified by the include/exclude properties of the second element (or the current workspace directory if not specified).

background.description: Patterns to track the begin and end of a matcher active on a background task.

activeOnStart.description: If set to true the background monitor starts in active mode. This is the same as outputting a line that matches beginsPattern when the task starts.

beginsPattern.description: If matched in the output the start of a background task is signaled.

endsPattern.description: If matched in the output the end of a background task is signaled.

watching.deprecationMessage: The watching property is deprecated. Use background instead.
watching.description: Patterns to track the begin and end of a watching matcher.

activeOnStart.description: If set to true the watcher starts in active mode. This is the same as outputting a line that matches beginsPattern when the task starts.

beginsPattern.description: If matched in the output the start of a watching task is signaled.

endsPattern.description: If matched in the output the end of a watching task is signaled.

name.description: The name of the problem matcher used to refer to it.

label.description: A human readable label of the problem matcher.

name.description: The name of the problem pattern.
The name of the problem multi line problem pattern.

profiles.description: Defines additional terminal profiles that the user can create.

id.description: The ID of the terminal profile provider.

icon.description: A codicon, URI, or light and dark URIs to associate with this terminal type.

titleTemplate.description: A title template string for the terminal tab. Supports variables like ${sequence}, ${process}, ${cwd}, etc. Overrides the default terminal.integrated.tabs.title setting for terminals created with this profile.

completionProviders.description: Defines terminal completion providers that will be registered when the extension activates.

description.description: A description of what the completion provider does. This will be shown in the settings UI.

id.description: The id of the authentication provider.

label.description: The human readable name of the authentication provider.

items.description: A list of globs that match the authorization servers that this provider supports.

authorizationServerGlobs.description: A list of globs that match the authorization servers that this provider supports.

languageId.description: Id of the language into which the display strings are translated.

languageName.description: Name of the language in English.

localizedLanguageName.description: Name of the language in contributed language.

translations.description: List of translations associated to the language.

id.description: Id of VS Code or Extension for which this translation is contributed to. Id of VS Code is always `vscode` and of extension should be in format `publisherId.extensionName`.
id.patternErrorMessage: Id should be `vscode` or in format `publisherId.extensionName` for translating VS code or an extension respectively.

path.description: A relative path to a file containing translations for the language.

id.description: A unique id for this chat participant.

name.description: User-facing name for this chat participant. The user will use '@' with this name to invoke the participant. Name must not contain whitespace.

fullName.markdownDescription: The full name of this chat participant, which is shown as the label for responses coming from this participant. If not provided, `name` is used.

description.description: A description of this chat participant, shown in the UI.

sampleRequest.description: When the user clicks this participant in `/help`, this text will be submitted to the participant.

when.description: A condition which must be true to enable this participant.

disambiguation.description: Metadata to help with automatically routing user questions to this chat participant.

description.description: A detailed description of the kinds of questions that are suitable for this chat participant.

examples.description: A list of representative example questions that are suitable for this chat participant.

commands.markdownDescription: Commands available for this chat participant, which the user can invoke with a `/`.

sampleRequest.description: When the user clicks this command in `/help`, this text will be submitted to the participant.

disambiguation.description: Metadata to help with automatically routing user questions to this chat command.

description.description: A detailed description of the kinds of questions that are suitable for this chat command.

examples.description: A list of representative example questions that are suitable for this chat command.

languageModelChatProviders.description: Contribute language model chat providers of a specific vendor.

mcpServerDefinitionProviders.description: Contributes Model Context Protocol servers. Users of this should also use `vscode.lm.registerMcpServerDefinitionProvider`.

when.description: Condition which must be true to enable this collection.

path.description: Path to the SKILL.md file relative to the extension root. The folder name must match the "name" property in SKILL.md.

allOf.description: Contributes a tool that can be invoked by a language model in a chat session, or from a standalone command. Registered tools can be used by all extensions.

name.description: A unique name for this tool. This name must be a globally unique identifier, and is also used as a name when presenting this tool to a language model.

toolReferenceName.markdownDescription: If `canBeReferencedInPrompt` is enabled for this tool, the user may use '#' with this name to invoke the tool in a query. Otherwise, the name is not required. Name must not contain whitespace.

displayName.description: A human-readable name for this tool that may be used to describe it in the UI.

userDescription.description: A description of this tool that may be shown to the user.

modelDescription.description: A description of this tool that may be used by a language model to select it.

inputSchema.description: A JSON schema for the input this tool accepts. The input must be an object at the top level. A particular language model may not support all JSON schema features. See the documentation for the language model family you are using for more information.

canBeReferencedInPrompt.markdownDescription: If true, this tool shows up as an attachment that the user can add manually to their request. Chat participants will receive the tool in `ChatRequest#toolReferences`.

icon.markdownDescription: An icon that represents this tool. Either a file path, an object with file paths for dark and light themes, or a theme icon reference, like "\$(zap)"

when.markdownDescription: Condition which must be true for this tool to be enabled. Note that a tool may still be invoked by another extension even when its `when` condition is false.

tags.description: A set of tags that roughly describe the tool's capabilities. A tool user may use these to filter the set of tools to just ones that are relevant for the task at hand, or they may want to pick a tag that can be used to identify just the tools contributed by this extension.

scheme.description: URI scheme on which to match the formatter on. For example "file". Simple glob patterns are supported.

authority.description: URI authority on which to match the formatter on. Simple glob patterns are supported.

formatting.description: Rules for formatting uri resource labels.

label.description: Label rules to display. For example: myLabel:/${path}. ${path}, ${scheme}, ${authority} and ${authoritySuffix} are supported as variables.

separator.description: Separator to be used in the uri label display. '/' or '' as an example.

stripPathStartingSeparator.description: Controls whether `${path}` substitutions should have starting separator characters stripped.

tildify.description: Controls if the start of the uri label should be tildified when possible.

workspaceSuffix.description: Suffix appended to the workspace label.

name.description: Name of the plugin as listed in the package.json.

enableForWorkspaceTypeScriptVersions.description: Should the plugin be loaded when using workspace versions of TypeScript?

id.markdownDescription: The identifier of the status bar entry. Must be unique within the extension. The same value must be used when calling the `vscode.window.createStatusBarItem(id, ...)`-API

name.description: The name of the entry, like 'Python Language Indicator', 'Git Status' etc. Try to keep the length of the name short, yet descriptive enough that users can understand what the status bar item is about.

text.description: The text to show for the entry. You can embed icons in the text by leveraging the `$(<name>)`-syntax, like 'Hello $(globe)!'

tooltip.description: The tooltip text for the entry.

command.description: The command to execute when the status bar entry is clicked.

alignment.description: The alignment of the status bar entry.

priority.description: The priority of the status bar entry. Higher value means the item should be shown more to the left.

accessibilityInformation.description: Defines the role and aria label to be used when the status bar entry is focused.

role.description: The role of the status bar entry which defines how a screen reader interacts with it. More about aria roles can be found here https://w3c.github.io/aria/#widget_roles

label.description: The aria label of the status bar entry. Defaults to the entry's text.

vendor.description: A globally unique vendor of language model chat provider.

configuration.description: Configuration options for the language model chat provider.

managementCommand.description: A command to manage the language model chat provider, e.g. 'Manage Copilot models'. This is used in the chat model picker. If not provided, a gear icon is not rendered during vendor selection.
managementCommand.deprecationMessage: The managementCommand property is deprecated and will be removed in a future release. Use the new configuration property instead.

deprecation.description: Marks this language model chat provider as deprecated. When set, the Manage Models view renders the provider with a link pointing to a replacement.

link.description: A URL opened when the user clicks the deprecation link shown next to the provider name. Use a 'vscode:extension/<publisher>.<name>' URI to open a replacement extension in the Extensions view.

when.description: Condition which must be true to show this language model chat provider in the Manage Models list.

workbench.editor.customLabels.patterns.markdownDescription:
Controls the rendering of the editor label. Each __Item__ is a pattern that matches a file path. Both relative and absolute file paths are supported. The relative path must include the WORKSPACE_FOLDER (e.g `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/src/**.tsx` or `*/src/**.tsx`). Absolute patterns must start with a `/`. In case multiple patterns match, the longest matching path will be picked. Each __Value__ is the template for the rendered editor when the __Item__ matches. Variables are substituted based on the context:
- `${dirname}`: name of the folder in which the file is located (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> folder`).
- `${dirname(N)}`: name of the nth parent folder in which the file is located (e.g. `N=2: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/static/folder/file.txt -> WORKSPACE_FOLDER`). Folders can be picked from the start of the path by using negative numbers (e.g. `N=-1: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> WORKSPACE_FOLDER`). If the __Item__ is an absolute pattern path, the first folder (`N=-1`) refers to the first folder in the absolute path, otherwise it corresponds to the workspace folder.
- `${filename}`: name of the file without the file extension (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> file`).
- `${extname}`: the file extension (e.g. `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.txt -> txt`).
- `${extname(N)}`: the nth extension of the file separated by '.' (e.g. `N=2: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.ext1.ext2.ext3 -> ext1`). Extension can be picked from the start of the extension by using negative numbers (e.g. `N=-1: WORKSPACE_FOLDER/folder/file.ext1.ext2.ext3 -> ext2`).

Example: `"**/static/**/*.html": "${filename} - ${dirname} (${extname})"` will render a file `WORKSPACE_FOLDER/static/folder/file.html` as `file - folder (html)`.

additionalProperties.markdownDescription: The template which should be rendered when the pattern matches. May include the variables ${dirname}, ${filename} and ${extname}.

enumDescriptions: Show the name of the file. When tabs are enabled and two files have the same name in one group the distinguishing sections of each file's path are added. When tabs are disabled, the path relative to the workspace folder is shown if the editor is active.
Show the name of the file followed by its directory name.
Show the name of the file followed by its path relative to the workspace folder.
Show the name of the file followed by its absolute path.

This editor displays its filename in italics on its tab or title label and in the Open Editors view. Its contents will be replaced by the next editor opened in preview mode. Making a change in a preview mode editor will persist it, as will a double-click on its label, or the 'Keep Open' option in its label context menu. workbench.editor.enablePreviewFromQuickO.markdownDescription: Controls whether editors opened from Quick Open show as preview editors. Preview editors do not stay open, and are reused until explicitly set to be kept open (via double-click or editing). When enabled, hold Ctrl before selection to open an editor as a non-preview. Preview editors do not stay open, and are reused until explicitly set to be kept open (via double-click or editing). Disabling this will keep the editor open  on such an event. By default, editors will open on the right hand side of the currently active one. If changed to `down`, the editors will open below the currently active one. workbench.editor.revealIfOpen.description: Controls whether an editor is revealed in any of the visible groups if opened. If disabled, an editor will prefer to open in the currently active editor group. If enabled, an already opened editor will be revealed instead of opened again in the currently active editor group. Note that there are some cases where this setting is ignored, such as when forcing an editor to open in a specific group or to the side of the currently active group.

workbench.layoutControl.type.description: Controls whether the layout control in the custom title bar is displayed as a single menu button or with multiple UI toggles.

window.title.markdownDescription:
Controls the window title based on the current context such as the opened workspace or active editor. Variables are substituted based on the context:
- `${activeEditorShort}`: the file name (e.g. myFile.txt).
- `${activeEditorMedium}`: the path of the file relative to the workspace folder (e.g. myFolder/myFileFolder/myFile.txt).
- `${activeEditorLong}`: the full path of the file (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder/myFileFolder/myFile.txt).
- `${activeEditorLanguageId}`: the language identifier of the active editor (e.g. typescript).
- `${activeFolderShort}`: the name of the folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFileFolder).
- `${activeFolderMedium}`: the path of the folder the file is contained in, relative to the workspace folder (e.g. myFolder/myFileFolder).
- `${activeFolderLong}`: the full path of the folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder/myFileFolder).
- `${folderName}`: name of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. myFolder).
- `${folderPath}`: file path of the workspace folder the file is contained in (e.g. /Users/Development/myFolder).
- `${rootName}`: name of the workspace with optional remote name and workspace indicator if applicable (e.g. myFolder, myRemoteFolder [SSH] or myWorkspace (Workspace)).
- `${rootNameShort}`: shortened name of the workspace without suffixes (e.g. myFolder, myRemoteFolder or myWorkspace).
- `${rootPath}`: file path of the opened workspace or folder (e.g. /Users/Development/myWorkspace).
- `${profileName}`: name of the profile in which the workspace is opened (e.g. Data Science (Profile)). Ignored if default profile is used.
- `${appName}`: e.g. VS Code.
- `${remoteName}`: e.g. SSH
- `${dirty}`: an indicator for when the active editor has unsaved changes.
- `${focusedView}`: the name of the view that is currently focused.
- `${activeRepositoryName}`: the name of the active repository (e.g. vscode).
- `${activeRepositoryBranchName}`: the name of the active branch in the active repository (e.g. main).
- `${activeEditorState}`: provides information about the state of the active editor (e.g. modified). This will be appended by default when in screen reader mode with `accessibility.windowTitleOptimized` enabled.
- `${separator}`: a conditional separator (" - ") that only shows when surrounded by variables with values or static text.

editor.semanticTokenColorCustomizations.description: Overrides editor semantic token color and styles from the currently selected color theme.

workbench.settings.enableNaturalLanguage.description: Controls whether to enable the natural language search mode for settings. The natural language search is provided by a Microsoft online service.

enumDescriptions: Hide the Table of Contents while searching.

workbench.settings.settingsSearchTocBeha.description: Controls the behavior of the Settings editor Table of Contents while searching. If this setting is being changed in the Settings editor, the setting will take effect after the search query is modified.

telemetry.performance.inputLatencySampli.markdownDescription: Probability (0 to 1) that input latency telemetry is reported for this session. Set to 0 to disable, 1 to always report.

notebook.lineNumbers.markdownDescription: Controls the display of line numbers in the cell editor.

inlineChat.notebookAgent.markdownDescription: Enable agent-like behavior for inline chat widget in notebooks.

inlineChat.affordance.description: Controls whether an inline chat affordance is shown when text is selected.
enumDescriptions: No affordance is shown.
Show an affordance in the editor at the cursor position.

inlineChat.fixDiagnostics.description: Controls whether the Fix action is shown for diagnostics in the editor.

inlineChat.askInChat.description: Controls whether files in a chat editing session use Ask in Chat instead of Inline Chat.

notebook.outline.showMarkdownHeadersOnly.markdownDescription: When enabled, notebook outline will show only markdown cells containing a header.

notebook.outline.showCodeCells.markdownDescription: When enabled, notebook outline shows code cells.

notebook.outline.showCodeCellSymbols.markdownDescription: When enabled, notebook outline shows code cell symbols. Relies on `#notebook.outline.showCodeCells#` being enabled.

notebook.breadcrumbs.showCodeCells.markdownDescription: When enabled, notebook breadcrumbs contain code cells.

notebook.gotoSymbols.showAllSymbols.markdownDescription: When enabled, the Go to Symbol Quick Pick will display full code symbols from the notebook, as well as Markdown headers.

notebook.navigation.allowNavigateToSurro.markdownDescription: When enabled cursor can navigate to the next/previous cell when the current cursor in the cell editor is at the first/last line.

notebook.diff.experimental.toggleInline.markdownDescription: Enable the command to toggle the experimental notebook inline diff editor.

notebook.displayOrder.description: Priority list for output mime types

notebook.cellToolbarLocation.description: Where the cell toolbar should be shown, or whether it should be hidden.

additionalProperties.markdownDescription: Configure the cell toolbar position for for specific file types

notebook.showCellStatusBar.description: Whether the cell status bar should be shown.
enumDescriptions: The cell status bar is always hidden.
The cell status bar is always visible.
The cell status bar is hidden until the cell has executed. Then it becomes visible to show the execution status.

notebook.cellExecutionTimeVerbosity.description: Controls the verbosity of the cell execution time in the cell status bar.
enumDescriptions: The cell execution duration is visible, with advanced information in the hover tooltip.
The cell last execution timestamp and duration are visible, with advanced information in the hover tooltip.

notebook.diff.enablePreview.description: Whether to use the enhanced text diff editor for notebook.

notebook.diff.overviewRuler.description: Whether to render the overview ruler in the diff editor for notebook.

notebook.cellToolbarVisibility.markdownDescription: Whether the cell toolbar should appear on hover or click.

notebook.undoRedoPerCell.description: Whether to use separate undo/redo stack for each cell.

notebook.compactView.description: Control whether the notebook editor should be rendered in a compact form. For example, when turned on, it will decrease the left margin width.

notebook.cellFocusIndicator.description: Controls where the focus indicator is rendered, either along the cell borders or on the left gutter.

notebook.insertToolbarLocation.description: Control where the insert cell actions should appear.
enumDescriptions: A toolbar that appears on hover between cells.
The toolbar at the top of the notebook editor.
Both toolbars.
The insert actions don't appear anywhere.

notebook.globalToolbar.description: Control whether to render a global toolbar inside the notebook editor.

notebook.stickyScroll.enabled.description: Experimental. Control whether to render notebook Sticky Scroll headers in the notebook editor.

notebook.stickyScroll.mode.description: Control whether nested sticky lines appear to stack flat or indented.
enumDescriptions: Nested sticky lines appear flat.
Nested sticky lines appear indented.

notebook.consolidatedOutputButton.description: Control whether outputs action should be rendered in the output toolbar.

notebook.showFoldingControls.description: Controls when the Markdown header folding arrow is shown.
enumDescriptions: The folding controls are always visible.
Never show the folding controls and reduce the gutter size.
The folding controls are visible only on mouseover.

notebook.dragAndDropEnabled.description: Control whether the notebook editor should allow moving cells through drag and drop.

notebook.consolidatedRunButton.description: Control whether extra actions are shown in a dropdown next to the run button.

notebook.globalToolbarShowLabel.description: Control whether the actions on the notebook toolbar should render label or not.

notebook.output.textLineLimit.markdownDescription: Controls how many lines of text are displayed in a text output. If `#notebook.output.scrolling#` is enabled, this setting is used to determine the scroll height of the output.

notebook.output.linkifyFilePaths.description: Control whether to disable filepath links in the output of notebook cells.

notebook.output.minimalErrorRendering.description: Control whether to render error output in a minimal style.

notebook.markup.fontSize.markdownDescription: Controls the font size in pixels of rendered markup in notebooks. When set to `0`, 120% of `#editor.fontSize#` is used.

notebook.markdown.lineHeight.markdownDescription: Controls the line height in pixels of markdown cells in notebooks. When set to `0`, `normal` will be used

notebook.editorOptionsCustomizations.description: Settings for code editors used in notebooks. This can be used to customize most editor.* settings.

editor.selectionClipboard.description: Controls whether the Linux primary clipboard should be supported.

interactiveWindow.collapseCellInputCode.markdownDescription: Controls whether code cells in the interactive window are collapsed by default.

notebook.output.lineHeight.markdownDescription:
Line height of the output text within notebook cells.
 - When set to 0, editor line height is used.
 - Values between 0 and 8 will be used as a multiplier with the font size.
 - Values greater than or equal to 8 will be used as effective values.

notebook.output.fontSize.markdownDescription: Font size for the output text within notebook cells. When set to 0, `#editor.fontSize#` is used.

notebook.output.fontFamily.markdownDescription: The font family of the output text within notebook cells. When set to empty, the `#editor.fontFamily#` is used.

notebook.output.scrolling.markdownDescription: Initially render notebook outputs in a scrollable region when longer than the limit.

notebook.output.wordWrap.markdownDescription: Controls whether the lines in output should wrap.

notebook.defaultFormatter.description: Defines a default notebook formatter which takes precedence over all other formatter settings. Must be the identifier of an extension contributing a formatter.

notebook.formatOnSave.enabled.markdownDescription: Format a notebook on save. A formatter must be available and the editor must not be shutting down. When `#files.autoSave#` is set to `afterDelay`, the file will only be formatted when saved explicitly.

notebook.insertFinalNewline.markdownDescription: When enabled, insert a final new line into the end of code cells when saving a notebook.

notebook.formatOnCellExecution.markdownDescription: Format a notebook cell upon execution. A formatter must be available.

notebook.confirmDeleteRunningCell.markdownDescription: Control whether a confirmation prompt is required to delete a running cell.

notebook.find.filters.markdownDescription: Customize the Find Widget behavior for searching within notebook cells. When both markup source and markup preview are enabled, the Find Widget will search either the source code or preview based on the current state of the cell.

notebook.experimental.remoteSave.markdownDescription: Enables the incremental saving of notebooks between processes and across Remote connections. When enabled, only the changes to the notebook are sent to the extension host, improving performance for large notebooks and slow network connections.

notebook.scrolling.revealNextCellOnExecu.markdownDescription: How far to scroll when revealing the next cell upon running notebook.cell.executeAndSelectBelow.
markdownEnumDescriptions: Scroll to fully reveal the next cell.
Scroll to reveal the first line of the next cell.

notebook.experimental.generate.markdownDescription: Enable experimental generate action to create code cell with inline chat enabled.

notebook.variablesView.markdownDescription: Enable the experimental notebook variables view within the debug panel.

notebook.inlineValues.markdownDescription: Control whether to show inline values within notebook code cells after cell execution. Values will remain until the cell is edited, re-executed, or explicitly cleared via the Clear All Outputs toolbar button or the `Notebook: Clear Inline Values` command.
enumDescriptions: Always show inline values, with a regex fallback if no inline value provider is registered. Note: There may be a performance impact in larger cells if the fallback is used.
Show inline values only when an inline value provider is registered.
Never show inline values.

notebook.cellFailureDiagnostics.markdownDescription: Show available diagnostics for cell failures.

notebook.backup.sizeLimit.markdownDescription: The limit of notebook output size in kilobytes (KB) where notebook files will no longer be backed up for hot reload. Use 0 for unlimited.

notebook.multiCursor.enabled.markdownDescription: Experimental. Enables a limited set of multi cursor controls across multiple cells in the notebook editor. Currently supported are core editor actions (typing/cut/copy/paste/composition) and a limited subset of editor commands.

notebook.markup.fontFamily.markdownDescription: Controls the font family of rendered markup in notebooks. When left blank, this will fall back to the default workbench font family.

chat.agents.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost.markdownDescription: When enabled, hides the Extension Host Copilot CLI entry from the Agents window picker. Requires `#chat.agentHost.enabled#`.

enumDescriptions: Use the built-in VS Code local chat harness
Use the Extension Host Copilot CLI
Use the Agent Host Copilot CLI
chat.editor.defaultProvider.description: Controls which provider is used as the default for new editor chat sessions.

chat.editor.localAgent.enabled.description: When enabled, shows the VS Code local chat harness in the chat picker.

chat.editor.copilotCli.hideExtensionHost.description: When enabled, hides the Extension Host Copilot CLI entry from the editor window chat picker.

chat.agentHost.enabled.description: When enabled, some agents run in a separate agent host process.

description.value: When enabled, some agents run in a separate agent host process.

chat.agentHost.claudeAgent.enabled.description: When enabled, the agent host registers the Claude provider (subject to the Claude SDK being reachable). Independent of `#chat.agents.claude.preferAgentHost#` and `#chat.editor.claude.preferAgentHost#`, which choose which integration surfaces Claude. Requires `#chat.agentHost.enabled#`. The agent host process must be restarted for changes to take effect.

description.value: Enable Claude Agent sessions in VS Code. Start and resume agentic coding sessions powered by Anthropic Claude Agent SDK directly in the editor. Uses your existing Copilot subscription.

chat.agentHost.byokModels.enabled.description: When enabled, the agent host wires up the BYOK ('bring your own key') language-model bridge so extension-provided BYOK models can run in agent-host sessions. Requires `#chat.agentHost.enabled#`. The agent host process must be restarted for changes to take effect.

chat.agentHost.codexAgent.enabled.description: When enabled, the agent host registers the Codex provider (subject to the Codex SDK being reachable). Requires `#chat.agentHost.enabled#`. The agent host process must be restarted for changes to take effect.

description.value: Enable Codex Agent sessions in VS Code. Start and resume agentic coding sessions powered by OpenAI Codex SDK. Uses your existing Copilot subscription.

chat.experimentalSessionsWindowOverride.description: When true, enables sessions-window-specific behavior for extensions.

chat.fontSize.description: Controls the font size in pixels in chat messages.

chat.fontFamily.description: Controls the font family in chat messages.

chat.editor.fontSize.description: Controls the font size in pixels in chat codeblocks.

chat.editor.fontFamily.description: Controls the font family in chat codeblocks.

chat.editor.fontWeight.description: Controls the font weight in chat codeblocks.

chat.editor.wordWrap.description: Controls whether lines should wrap in chat codeblocks.

chat.editor.lineHeight.description: Controls the line height in pixels in chat codeblocks. Use 0 to compute the line height from the font size.

enumDescriptions: The agent status indicator is hidden from the title bar.
Shows the agent status as a badge next to the command center.
Replaces the command center search box with a compact agent status indicator and unified chat widget.
chat.agentsControl.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls how the 'Agent Status' indicator appears in the title bar command center. When set to `hidden`, the indicator is not shown. Other values show the indicator and automatically enable `#window.commandCenter#`. The unread and in-progress session indicators require `#chat.viewSessions.enabled#` to be enabled.

chat.unifiedAgentsBar.enabled.markdownDescription: Replaces the command center search box with a unified chat and search widget.

chat.agentSessionProjection.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls whether Agent Session Projection mode is enabled for reviewing agent sessions in a focused workspace.

chat.implicitContext.enabled.description: Enables automatically using the active editor as chat context for specified chat locations.

additionalProperties.description: The value for the implicit context.
enumDescriptions: Implicit context is never enabled.
Implicit context is enabled for the first interaction.
Implicit context is always enabled.

chat.implicitContext.suggestedContext.markdownDescription: Controls whether the new implicit context flow is shown. In Ask and Edit modes, the context will automatically be included. When using an agent, context will be suggested as an attachment. Selections are always included as context.

chat.implicitContext.includeActiveEditor.markdownDescription:
When enabled, the active editor is automatically forwarded as context, even when it would otherwise only be suggested. Selections and explicitly attached files are always included regardless of this setting.

Note: this setting currently only applies to Agent Host sessions (such as the Copilot CLI).

chat.editing.autoAcceptDelay.markdownDescription: Delay after which changes made by chat are automatically accepted. Values are in seconds, `0` means disabled and `100` seconds is the maximum.

chat.editing.explainChanges.enabled.markdownDescription: Controls whether the Explain button in the Chat panel and the Explain Changes context menu in the SCM view are shown. This is an experimental feature.

chat.editing.revealNextChangeOnResolve.markdownDescription: Controls whether the editor automatically reveals the next change after keeping or undoing a chat edit.

chat.editing.openChangedFileInDiffEditor.markdownDescription: Controls whether selecting a file in the changed files list of a chat response opens it in a diff editor showing the changes made by chat, or in a regular editor. Holding `kbstyle(Alt)` while selecting the file opens it with the opposite behavior.

enumDescriptions: No animation is shown.
Shows a confetti burst animation around the thumbs up button.
Shows floating thumbs up icons rising from the button.
Shows expanding pulse rings from the button.
Shows radiant lines emanating from the button.
chat.upvoteAnimation.description: Controls whether an animation is shown when clicking the thumbs up button on a chat response.

chat.experimental.detectParticipant.enab.deprecationMessage: This setting is deprecated. Please use `chat.detectParticipant.enabled` instead.
chat.experimental.detectParticipant.enab.description: Enables chat participant autodetection for panel chat.

chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.e.description: Enables incremental rendering with optional block-level animation when streaming chat responses.

enumDescriptions: No animation. Content appears instantly.
Simple opacity fade from 0 to 1.
Content fades in while rising upward.
Content fades in from a blurred state.
Content scales up from slightly smaller.
Content slides in from the left.
Content reveals top-to-bottom with a soft gradient edge.
chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.a.description: Controls the animation style for incremental rendering.

enumDescriptions: Renders content immediately as tokens arrive.
Reveals content word by word.
Buffers content until a paragraph break before rendering.
chat.experimental.incrementalRendering.b.description: Controls how content is buffered before rendering during incremental rendering. Lower buffering levels render faster but may show incomplete sentences or partially formed markdown.

chat.detectParticipant.enabled.description: Enables chat participant autodetection for panel chat.

enumDescriptions: Display file and symbol references as boxed widgets with icons.
Display file and symbol references as simple blue links without icons.
chat.inlineReferences.style.description: Controls how file and symbol references are displayed in chat messages.

chat.editorAssociations.markdownDescription: Configure [glob patterns](https://aka.ms/vscode-glob-patterns) to editors for opening files from chat (for example `"*.md": "vscode.markdown.preview.editor"`).

enumDescriptions: Never show OS notifications for confirmations.
Show OS notifications for confirmations when the window is not focused.
Always show OS notifications for confirmations, even when the window is focused.
chat.notifyWindowOnConfirmation.description: Controls whether a chat session should present the user with an OS notification when a confirmation or question needs input. This includes a window badge as well as notification toast.

chat.autopilot.advanced.enabled.markdownDescription: Enables **Advanced Autopilot**, a single switch that turns on all advanced Autopilot behaviors that delegate more of the loop to the agent. Currently, after each Autopilot turn a small, fast model evaluates whether your original request is complete; if not, Autopilot keeps working using that evaluation as guidance for the next turn, instead of relying on the agent to signal completion itself.

chat.planReview.inlineEditor.enabled.markdownDescription: When enabled, the plan review widget mounts an editor inline, as opposed to in a separate editor tab.

enumDescriptions: Start new chat sessions with Default Approvals.
Start new chat sessions in Bypass Approvals mode.
Start new chat sessions in Autopilot mode.
chat.permissions.default.description: Controls the default permissions picker mode for new local chat sessions. You can still change the permission mode per session, and each session remembers the permission mode that was used. If enterprise policy disables auto approval, new sessions use Default Approvals.

chat.experimental.permissionsSandboxTogg.markdownDescription: Controls whether the permissions picker shows an inline "Sandboxing for terminal" toggle on the Default Approvals option. The toggle reflects and updates `#chat.agent.sandbox.enabled#`.

enumDescriptions: Interactive — step-by-step collaboration.
Plan — plan first, execute when ready.
Autopilot — autonomously iterate from start to finish.
mode.description: The starting mode for new agent sessions.

enumDescriptions: Default Approvals — Copilot uses your configured settings.
Bypass Approvals — all tool calls are auto-approved.
approvals.description: The starting approval behavior for new agent sessions. If enterprise policy disables auto approval, new sessions use Default Approvals.

chat.defaultConfiguration.markdownDescription: Controls the default configuration for new agent sessions (such as Copilot CLI). You can still change the mode and approval behavior per session, and each session remembers what was used.

chat.defaultModel.markdownDescription: The default model for new chat conversations. Use "auto" to let Copilot pick a model, a model family name (such as "opus" or "gemini") to use the latest available model in that family, or a full model id. You can still switch the model within a conversation; each new conversation starts at this model.

description.value: Sets the default chat model for new conversations. Accepts "auto", a model family name (such as "opus" or "gemini"), or a full model id. Users can still switch the model within a conversation.

chat.sessionSync.enabled.markdownDescription: Enable session sync to GitHub.com. When enabled, Copilot session data is synced to your GitHub account for cross-device access and richer insights. Requires `#github.copilot.chat.localIndex.enabled#` to also be enabled.

description.value: Enable session sync to GitHub.com for cross-device Copilot session history. When disabled by organization policy, session data is kept local only.

chat.sessionSync.excludeRepositories.markdownDescription: Repository patterns to exclude from session sync. Use exact `owner/repo` names or glob patterns like `my-org/*`. Sessions from matching repositories will only be stored locally.

chat.tools.edits.autoApprove.markdownDescription:
Controls whether edits made by the agent are automatically approved. The default is to approve all edits except those made to certain files which have the potential to cause immediate unintended side-effects, such as `**/.vscode/*.json`.

Set to `true` to automatically approve edits to matching files, `false` to always require explicit approval. The last pattern matching a given file will determine whether the edit is automatically approved.

chat.tools.urls.autoApprove.markdownDescription:
Controls which URLs are automatically approved when requested by chat tools. Keys are URL patterns and values can be `true` to approve both requests and responses, `false` to deny, or an object with `approveRequest` and `approveResponse` properties for granular control.

Examples:
- `"https://example.com": true` - Approve all requests to example.com
- `"https://*.example.com": true` - Approve all requests to any subdomain of example.com
- `"https://example.com/api/*": { "approveRequest": true, "approveResponse": false }` - Approve requests but not responses for example.com/api paths

chat.tools.eligibleForAutoApproval.markdownDescription: Controls which tools are eligible for automatic approval. Tools set to 'false' will always present a confirmation and will never offer the option to auto-approve. The default behavior (or setting a tool to 'true') may result in the tool offering auto-approval options.

enumDescriptions: askQuestions - Ask structured clarifying questions using single select, multi-select, or freeform inputs to collect task requirements before proceeding.
createAndRunTask - Create and run a task in the workspace
extensions - Search for VS Code extensions
getTaskOutput - Get Task Output
getTerminalOutput - Get Terminal Output
killTerminal - Kill Terminal
